title: The public site
caption: Where both sides arrive. One product, two doors: Find Work and Post a Job.

title: Worker signup — role toggle
caption: Find Work is selected. Worker and Client are the same table with a role flag, so the toggle is the only difference at this point.

title: Worker signup — details entered
caption: Name, phone, email, password. The password is bcrypt-hashed before it is stored; nothing here is kept in plain text.

title: Phone OTP requested
caption: A 6-digit code was generated, hashed, stored with a 10-minute expiry and 5-attempt cap, then sent. In this build the provider is the mock, so the code is written to the server console.

title: Phone OTP entered
caption: The code from the mock SMS. Swap SMS_PROVIDER to twilio or fast2sms in .env and this exact step sends a real text — no other code changes.

title: Waiting on the email link
caption: Phone is verified. Email is optional to continue but required before applying, so the flow nudges rather than blocks.

title: Email verification link opened
caption: The link from the mock inbox, opened in a second tab exactly as a user would. The waiting tab notices and moves itself on.

title: Worker profile — experience and charges
caption: This is the step your brief calls out: the worker publishes what they've done and what they charge, per hour and per week. Both numbers are reference rates — the binding figure is the one agreed on the job.

title: Identity verification (KYC)
caption: Tier ladder: Unverified → Basic → Verified → Trusted. Nothing touching money is reachable below Verified. The documents are mocked here and auto-approve; a real KYC/AML provider drops into the same call.

title: Worker dashboard
caption: The worker is live: verified phone, verified email, Verified KYC tier, a published profile and published charges.

title: Client signup — Post a Job
caption: Same form, other door. Choosing Business adds the company fields.

title: Client signup — business details
caption: Company name and registration number are captured up front so the contract can name a legal entity rather than a person.

title: Client phone OTP
caption: Identical verification path for both sides — a client who can post work is as verified as a worker who can take it.

title: Client OTP entered
caption: Codes are single-use: verifying marks the token consumed, so a replayed code fails.

title: Client email pending
caption: Email is required before posting a job, which is why the client is walked through it now.

title: Client email verified
caption: One click from the inbox. The token is hashed at rest and expires in an hour.

title: Client profile setup
caption: Address is stored but never shown publicly — jobs only ever advertise an area.

title: Client verified
caption: The client also has to clear KYC — funding escrow is gated on it, and the gate is checked server-side in fundPhaseAction, not just hidden in the UI.

title: Post a job — step 1, basics
caption: Title, a real specification, and a category. The description becomes the contract's scope clause verbatim, so vagueness here is expensive later.

title: Post a job — step 2, role line items
caption: One post can hire a whole crew: each role carries its own headcount and per-person rate, and the budget auto-sums. Here it's a single Android developer at ₹1,20,000.

title: Post a job — step 3, logistics
caption: Only the area is published. The exact address is released after a hire exists.

title: Post a job — step 4, funding mode
caption: Fund-at-hire is the honest choice for a phased project: the client funds phase by phase rather than parking the whole budget up front.

title: Post a job — step 5, review
caption: Everything the worker will see, before it goes live.

title: The job is live
caption: Published. It is now visible in every worker's Find Jobs, filtered by skill and area.

title: Find Jobs
caption: The client's post, seconds old, in the worker's feed.

title: The job as the worker reads it
caption: Full spec, the per-person rate, open slots, and the client's verification badge. Trust is symmetrical — the worker is checking the client out too.

title: Applying
caption: Cover note plus a rate. The rate pre-fills from the posting and is negotiable — what the worker types here becomes the contract total if they're hired.

title: Application submitted
caption: Tracked on the worker's side from the moment it's sent.

title: The applicant, as the client sees them
caption: Rating, jobs completed, years of experience, and the charges the worker published at signup — hourly and weekly — next to what they've quoted for this specific job.

title: Milestone plan — the suggested split
caption: Accepting doesn't create a hire on its own. First the client turns ₹1,20,000 into a payment schedule. The app suggests phases that fit software work; every field is editable.

title: Milestone plan — the agreed split
caption: Five phases, front-light and back-loaded on the risky integration work. The running total has to land exactly on the agreed value; the server re-checks the sum, so a plan that doesn't balance can't create a hire.

title: The generated contract
caption: Parties, engagement, scope, the five-phase payment schedule, and ten fixed escrow/dispute clauses — generated from the hire, not typed by anyone. The SHA-256 under it is what the signatures bind to.

title: Client signing
caption: The signature is the party's full legal name, typed. The server checks it against the verified account name, so you can't sign as someone else.

title: Client signed — one of two
caption: Recorded with a timestamp and the signer's network address. Escrow is still locked: one signature is not a contract.

title: Worker's hire — signature pending
caption: The worker sees the hire and a blocking banner. Nothing is funded and no work is expected until they've read the terms.

title: The same document, worker side
caption: Byte-identical text and an identical hash — both sides render from one function, so the two parties provably cannot be shown different terms.

title: Fully executed
caption: Both signatures recorded against the same SHA-256. Change one rupee in the schedule now and the recomputed hash stops matching — the app flags the contract as void rather than silently accepting it.

title: Client wallet — before any funding
caption: A custodial wallet was provisioned at signup: a real on-chain address the platform holds the key for. The client never sees a key or pays gas, and the balance is shown in rupees.

title: Mock fiat on-ramp
caption: ₹10,000 credited. In this build that's the platform relayer minting a test ERC-20 (cwINR) to the client's address — a real transaction on a test chain, standing in for a UPI/card payment that a processor would convert to stablecoin.

title: Phase tracker — nothing funded yet
caption: Five phases, sequential. Only phase 1 offers a Fund button; the rest say funding unlocks when the previous phase closes, and the server enforces the same rule.

title: Phase 1 funded — ₹15,000 in escrow
caption: Paid through the payment window from the client's ChainWork wallet: approve, then fundPhase — two on-chain transactions, and a receipt. The money has left the client's wallet and sits in the PhaseEscrow contract. Neither party can pull it out unilaterally.

title: Worker sees the money is locked
caption: This is the point of the whole design: the worker starts phase 1 knowing ₹15,000 is already locked and can only go to them or back to the client by a rule, not by the client's mood.

title: Phase 1 delivered
caption: The worker marks delivery. That opens the client's verification window — two working days, weekends and configured holidays skipped — and the same deadline is written into the smart contract, which refuses an early auto-release.

title: Client's verification window
caption: Approve and release, request changes (twice at most), or escalate. Doing nothing is also an outcome — see phase 3.

title: Release
caption: The Forge Complete moment. approveRelease fires on-chain and the escrow pays the worker's payout address in the same transaction.

title: Phase 1 closed — phase 2 unlocked
caption: Released, irreversibly. Phase 2's Fund button appears only now.

title: The worker's money
caption: ₹15,000, an on-chain balance read live from the token contract — not a number in our database. The transaction row carries the real hash.

title: Phase 2 funded — ₹25,000
caption: Exactly the pattern your brief describes: the client tops the next phase up only after the previous one closed. Total exposure at any moment is one phase, never the whole ₹1,20,000.

title: Changes requested
caption: Not everything is a dispute. Two revision rounds are built in; each one resets the verification window on redelivery. After the second, the app pushes you to a complaint instead of an endless loop.

title: Redelivered
caption: The escrow never moved during the revision — it stayed locked the whole time.

title: Phase 2 released — ₹40,000 paid to date
caption: Two of five closed.

title: Phase 3 delivered — and then nothing
caption: Now the client stops responding. On most platforms this is where a freelancer loses a month chasing an invoice.

title: Reminders, capped
caption: The timing worker sends a bounded number of nudges — two by default, configurable by an admin. It is not a nagging loop; it's a countdown with a defined end.

title: Auto-released
caption: The window lapsed with the reminders spent, so the escrow paid out on its own — the smart contract's autoRelease, which reverts if called even a second early. Silence is not leverage.

title: ₹70,000 received across three phases
caption: Two approved by the client, one released by the clock. Same destination either way.

title: Phase 4 released
caption: ₹1,00,000 of ₹1,20,000 settled. One phase left.

title: All five phases released
caption: The tracker is fully green and the hire flips to Completed automatically once the last phase settles — which is what opens up reviews.

title: Client reviews the worker
caption: Only reachable on a completed hire, once per direction, by the actual party. A client→worker review recomputes the worker's public rating and their sub-scores.

title: Worker reviews the client
caption: Reputation is two-sided. The client's escrow-reliability score is derived from funding behaviour, not opinion.

title: ₹1,20,000 earned
caption: The full contract value, in the worker's own on-chain wallet, with a transaction row and hash per phase.

title: Withdrawn — the off-ramp
caption: The balance really leaves the wallet: a genuine on-chain transfer out of custody. In this build the destination is the platform's off-ramp sink; in production that call is replaced by a payment processor paying INR into the worker's bank account or UPI ID.

title: The worker's profile after one project
caption: Rating, completed-job count and the published charges — the reputation this contract just earned, which is what gets them the next one.
